items.transkript: Good morning. Good morning. Good  morning. Good morning to the beautiful  people of our beautiful country. The  crow started before even having its  breakfast. Today is Tuesday, October 6.  It is Tuesday, October 6, and our  agenda is still the biggest corruption,  the biggest theft, the biggest fraud in  the history of the Republic of Turkey.  We are talking about the Ponzi scheme.  You know, we keep saying it over and  over every day. It is a heist of  approximately 20 billion dollars, a 20  billion dollar heist. When you convert  it to Turkish Lira, it is a 900 billion  TL heist. There are 500,000 direct  victims. When you look at the stock  market as a whole, it is a massive  scandal that concerns 5 million people  including their families and has caused  5 million people to lose money. It is  no longer about stealing money through  tenders, bribes, or from a treasury or  a safe, but a system of corruption, a  corruption order where they directly  defraud the citizens, and there is  still a huge darkness surrounding it.  More than two weeks have passed.  Despite more than two weeks passing, we  still do not have the list of these  fraudsters in our hands. The government , the economic management, the  prosecutor's office, the palace, and  the politicians know who these  fraudsters are, but it is not disclosed  to the public. It is being hidden from  the public. This is truly a picture  that reveals that the promise that this  robbery will be brought to light, that  they will go to the end as the  government says, and even that "no  matter who it touches" is just empty  rhetoric. Because they are not  disclosing it. Now, there is a latest  calculation. Economist Sabri Öncü.  Sabri Öncü did a calculation. He  examined the tables and published the  table. On his social media account,  look, the total value of these  independent portfolio management  company funds was 349 billion 638  million liras on September 16, that is,  one day before the heist. Look, one day  later, on September 17, it dropped to  122 billion 511 million liras. He  published this table himself, and there  is a picture of a huge theft here.  There is a picture of a huge theft in  this table. And now he says that a  total of 227 billion liras have been  withdrawn from the funds. But there is  a reset procedure here. Since the funds  were seized, we don't know if that  exact number is valid. There are  hesitations regarding this issue. But  it is a fact that there are 650  accounts. 650 accounts carried out a  massive operation, a flight, and sold  their shares with huge amounts— billions, tens of billions, and even  hundreds of billions of liras—right  before the heist, that is, before the  16th of September. How did they do this ? You know they inflated the shares in  these funds, and all state institutions  actually exist in the economy to  prevent those shares from being  inflated, to prevent small companies  from rising to the value of Tüpraş,  or to prevent absurd situations like  Özata Denizcilik surpassing Arçelik  or the Koç Group; for example, so that  Gündoğdu Gıda, a shut-down factory  in Turkey that doesn't even have a cow  inside and has only two employees,  doesn't become one of Turkey's most  valuable companies, or rather, doesn't  appear to be one. There is the Capital  Markets Board to supervise. It  supervises every day, or the BDDK  decides on whether or not to grant  banking licenses to these funds. For  instance, there is Borsa Istanbul. It  sees those shares, the inflated shares.  It is happening right before their eyes . They never touched them. These funds  were inflated, inflated, inflated. Then , with the approval of state  institutions, they went public, clearly  intending to pull off a scam. Meaning,  state institutions gave permission. The  Capital Markets Board (SPK) gave  permission. Borsa Istanbul turned a  blind eye, and thousands, hundreds of  thousands of people rushed into this  trap. Then they sold. On September 16,  they took the money and left. Now  economist Sabri Öncü says there are  650 people there. And he asks who these  650 people are. As you know, we keep  asking, but we never get an answer.  Actually, as we said, all these names  were known from the very first day;  look, even when the scandal broke— meaning the day the system collapsed— the state did not intervene. The system  collapsed, meaning these funds  defaulted. And only then did this  incident come to light. Otherwise,  there was no operation anywhere. They  waited for the system to collapse while  the public was being fleeced. They  watched. During that process—the  process where the public was being  fleeced and they watched until the end —they saw on September 17 that the  stock market had crashed. There were  already very sharp drops in the stock  market. It was announced that the funds  would be liquidated. They were seized  and trading was halted. And that day,  the entire economic management, the  palace, and the AKP had the list of  those who committed this scam, and for  two weeks they haven't disclosed that  list to us. Do you know how many people  are involved in Tera? In Tera, before  the IPO. I mean, right when they were  going to scam people and take it public . When the SPK gave approval, there  were 159 investors. Those 159 investors  are the ones who inflated those shares,  the ones who set the trap. And then  they are the ones who made the killing.  They don't explain that either. I mean,  those 159 are also included in the 650.  So, if you look at it, the scheme here  seems to involve about 600-700 people.  Now, you might ask how many are in  custody. When you look at the number of  detainees, there are 85 people in  custody. There are 98 people released  under judicial control. The total  number of suspects is 217. Now, when  you subtract this from that 650— meaning when you subtract 217—it  turns out there are over 400 people  being hidden and concealed. Over 400  people emerge. Why are these people  being hidden? These scammers, are these  companies now—I mean, there are also  those who taught them how to run these  companies after all. Why are they being  hidden? Why are they not being  announced to the public? Look, they  persistently refuse to disclose them.  And then they say we will go to the end . Erdoğan is very angry, Erdoğan is  very furious. It is said that they will  go to the end. Now, some calculations  are even being made regarding these 650  people. Of course, these are  controversial calculations, but it is  reported that they made off with  hundreds of millions of liras per  person. It is said that they made a  killing, but it is not enough that they  won't disclose these 650 people. Look,  we know some of those 650 people, right ? For example, Fatma Betüshan Kaya, or  "Ponzi Fatma," is one of them; she  alone swindled 2 billion TL, 2.2  billion TL from people. But it's not  just her. We will talk about that in a  moment. There are other names within  that 650, but there are very important,  very powerful names that still haven't  been disclosed. Everyone knows this.  Everyone is saying this. There are  people who are very powerful in the  bureaucracy, very powerful in politics —very powerful people everywhere. Now , looking at this, specifically at  Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, a very  important development occurred late  yesterday evening. They were saying,  you know, that she had returned the  money she had made, uh, something like  that. Then it turned out she hadn't  returned it. There was no such thing,  it turns out. I mean, like, "I earned  this money," and so on. She was just  crying. She was crying. And now Eren is  bringing up the footage as well. It’s  not just that money. I mean, the 2.2  billion TL heist there isn't all of it.  It turns out they have been bleeding  the country dry for years. Do you want  villas, do you want mansions? Mansions  worth 200, 300 million TL each.  Apartments in skyscrapers, plots of  land with her family—incredible plots . All these assets worth 250-300  million TL have also been exposed.  Yiğit Uzun had shared these. There is  no denial whatsoever. He brought them  to light. Now they are saying, as of  yesterday, the Demirören News Agency  shared some information. It turns out  Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, "Fund-Fatma,"  and her husband İlyas Kaya have  returned the money. They returned the  money. Look, think of it based on a  voluntary basis like this. You rob a  bank. You run away with the money. You  put the money into an interest-bearing  account. For two weeks, nobody knows,  well, everyone knows you robbed it. " Fund-Fatma" went into the bank, said " hands up," took the money, and went  home with 2.2 billion TL. Remember that  mansion you saw a moment ago? Let's say  she went to that mansion. It was  registered under her mother’s name,  too. In Büyükçekmece. This is an  ultra-luxury complex. She sat there.  She put the money in a bank. She robbed  one and put it in another bank. She  might have even put it in the bank she  robbed. Then, she collected 2 million  TL in interest every day. Look, she  collected 2 million TL in daily  interest. Then two weeks passed. For  two weeks, the police didn't knock on  her door. Nobody said, "Come give a  statement," or anything. Nobody took  action. Absolutely nobody took action.  This was 2.2 billion TL. Then she said,  "I will return it." Look at what she  did. Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya and her  husband İlyas Kaya. Apart from the  principal, 163 million TL of the  principal, they were voluntary—so  they say. They returned it to the SDIF  (TMSF). They wanted to do it  voluntarily. They returned it  voluntarily. Now, according to the  Capital Markets Board (SPK) law, people  are required to pay twice the benefit  they obtained when returning funds. Now , there is something very critical here . There is a very critical situation.  First of all, weren't their assets  frozen? It had been announced. It was  announced that Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya  and her husband İlyas Kaya's assets  were frozen. Meaning it was announced  they were seized. But then how can they  return that money? If their assets are  already frozen, they shouldn't be able  to return that money. What does this  mean? It means there is no  investigation against them. Because the  only point that made us think there was  an investigation was this. The seizure  of their assets. If assets are seized,  it means they are suspects. But they  never make an official statement about  this either. They were leaking  information. They were pretending as if  there was an investigation. Now, since  it is known that this was returned, I  don't know, maybe there is some other  procedure, but if they can return that  money voluntarily, it means it wasn't  seized. They gave it willingly. I mean,  there is also another situation here. I  mean, the law is very clear. Look, the  law is very clear. I mean, it is  included in articles 107/1 and 107/3 of  Law No. 6362. It says they have to  complete the 15-day period as well.  After the board's decision, the board  had announced that you could deposit  money there voluntarily. Look at who  they are saving. They are shielding men  from investigation. They are shielding  women from investigation. They are  shielding politicians from  investigation. They are shielding  bureaucrats from investigation. And  these people went and returned it.  Actually, they need to pay 4.4 billion  TL. The Capital Markets Board law is  very clear. They need to return double  the amount. But they say "that's enough ." They aren't even paying the  principal amount. They are not paying  the 163 million TL. Where did you find  the 163 million TL, Fatma Hanım? I  wonder where "Fund Fatma" found the 163  million TL? Now when you look at it, I  mean, during this process of 2 weeks,  they must have earned a very serious  amount of interest from that money. I  mean, think about 2 million per day,  multiply it by 2 weeks, they made tens  of millions of lira in interest. Anyway , she didn't return the scholarship  money she received unlawfully from the  Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality back  in 2009 when the AKP ran it. She took  that scholarship money back then and  didn't pay it back. I guess she will  pocket all the interest too. You might  say, "Well, interest is forbidden for  them," or something. I would say, "For  God's sake, don't mock me; it was  supposed to be forbidden." The woman  and her husband swindled thousands of  people. They pulled off a very  significant 2.2 billion TL heist, but I  guess we still won't call it that. Look . I mean, it is truly very interesting.  I mean, will a step be taken regarding  this? Will they not be investigated?  Really, look, these moves are moves to  avoid investigation. These are "cover  it up, they paid the money, let's close  the file" moves. These moves also align  perfectly with not taking their  statements. They were saying, "Erdoğan  is very angry, he will go to the end,  everyone will be held accountable,"  right? Everyone is reporting things  like that. Loyalists are everywhere.  Erdoğan was very angry. Everyone will  be held accountable. No, friends, this  is exactly about how these people won't  be held accountable. These are moves to  quell the reactions. These are moves to  cover it up. These are absolute  cover-up moves. I mean, this means the  following. It means Fatma Betüsankaya  will not be called in to testify. She  committed this crime. She was caught  red-handed. She was caught with the  records. She was caught with documents,  one by one. But it means she won't be  detained. It means she won't be  arrested. If this were in any  opposition municipality, let alone any  ordinary person, if you defrauded  people of 2.2 billion TL, you would  wake up in prison. But these people are  blue-blooded. As a whole country, we  cannot satisfy them. A handful of  people, the whole country cannot  satisfy them. They also have these  immunity-from-punishment statuses.  These are the blue-blooded, untouchable  people of this country. These are the  untouchable people of this country. Now , of course, we say she won't testify.  Why are they not going towards her  testifying? They aren't taking that  path. Now, the question on everyone's  mind. Now, if you see someone on the  street, see them under arrest, you say,  "Man, Fatma is free, 'Ponzi' Fatma is  free, how is this person inside?"  Everyone is saying this. Everyone's  trust in the justice system was already  at rock bottom. It’s completely  buried now, at zero, zero, below zero.  But look, because she could talk. I  tell this story all the time, I say it  over and over, and I will keep saying  it tirelessly. This is the system  itself. Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya cannot  be made to talk in a case that is the  system itself. She cannot talk. If she  talks, the system will be exposed. This  is the system itself. This is a picture  of how a handful of people under the  AKP government are robbing the public.  If the government investigates and  uncovers this, that scandal will grow  tenfold. If the names behind this, this  powerful structure, this organized  crime syndicate, this very powerful  structure—which stops investigations,  halts economic management, and to whom  even the Minister of Treasury and  Finance has to defer—is exposed, the  AKP government won't stand a chance of  staying in power; that’s why they  have to cover it up. That’s why they  want to pay the money and close this as  soon as possible. The story of let’s  not judge any of them. Look, that is  exactly what is happening. Fatma Betül  Sayan Kaya speaks to Nagehan Alçı.  Look, she says the entire conversation  is off the record. Hadi Özışık had  done the same thing. She only allows  one sentence. Look, she only allows one  sentence. Do you know what it is?  Alçı, tell it. She had something to  say about not being alone in this. But  she wasn't in a mood like "I'll give  other names out of spite." She had  something to say about not being alone  in this. Do you know what this means? I  will talk. I will tell on you too. She  says, "I am not alone.""I am not alone. " Think about how big and how powerful  the organization is that it is covering  up this investigation. No one is angry  either. No one is in the mood to get to  the bottom of this. And it doesn't end  there; not only is her statement not  being taken. Because as you know, Ponzi  Fatma is bigger than Turkey. Much  bigger than Turkey. They won't even  take Ponzi Fatma's statement. And do  you know what she's doing during this  time? Why are others taken into custody ? In operations involving opposition  municipalities, people say, "They might  destroy the evidence." They say  there’s a risk of flight and so on.  They say, "They might destroy the  evidence." Meanwhile, Fatma Büsayan is  deleting the evidence. Right in front  of everyone's eyes, she is deleting her  Instagram posts. Now, Yıldır Uğur  prepared a report. I will ask Eren for  the footage from that report. There are  pictures on Instagram. Do you know who  she is with? Look, these pictures are  from a Roma event. An event held in  Istanbul by the AKP Istanbul Provincial  Presidency. Do you know who is next to  her? Erdin Özel, the chairman of the  board of Ptero Portföy, a former AKP  member responsible for economic affairs . Erdin Özel. She makes reports around  Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya. They were  saying, "What does it have to do with  her, she has no connection," and so on.  They weren't even confirming it. They  were saying she had nothing to do with  it. Look, friends, how powerful the  organization is. Look, we see it right  here. They only placed a travel ban on  Erdin Özel. Look, a heist is being  pulled off at the portfolio, at Tere  Portfolio. Emre Tezmen is being  arrested as the owner of that place,  the Alkin brothers are being arrested,  they are in the management of that  place, and so on. The chairman of the  board of directors at the head of the  portfolio is only given a travel ban.  That's how he's being protected. Then,  when there was public outcry and Foncu  Fatma, or "Fonzi Fatma," was exposed,  they had to arrest Erdin Özel. Erdin  Özel is such a key, such a pivotal  point. Now, do you know what day these  photos you see on the screen were taken ? They were taken on April 8th. They  met at a Roma meeting. Look, the  Istanbul Provincial Chair is there.  Erdin Özel doesn't normally have an  official role, but he is sitting right  next to Fonzi Fatma. Everyone was  already saying it. They always work  side by side, together. They do  business together. The manager of  Teraport, the chairman of the board, is  this open, and should I tell you  something even more? It is so blatant,  do you know what they are doing on  April 8th? What is happening on April  8th? Fatma is buying the stocks she  manipulated. "Foncu Fatma," this is  exactly during this meeting, the photo  from the day of the incident, the  moment of the murder. The murder, like  holding a gun, right about to pull the  trigger, do you know who else is next  to her at that moment? The Istanbul  Provincial Chair is there. One wonders,  with the Istanbul Provincial Chair  right on the other side, did he buy  some too? After all, they must have  given him a tip on April 8th. Even if  they didn't give a tip, he must be  asking. They are making multi-billion  transactions at that moment. They are  pulling off a 2.2 billion TL heist.  They aren't telling the person next to  them. I mean, that's what happened. Who  else is close to Erdin Özel, I wonder?  Are Erdin Özel's HTS records, base  station signals, and such being checked ? They always check those in  investigations, right? Is the garden of  his father's house being dug up? Are  his children's piggy banks being seized ? Are his children's cartoon CDs being  confiscated? Was the whole house  searched? Were his digital materials  confiscated? Does he have  correspondence, for example? WhatsApp  messages. Look, they aren't even taking  Fatma Betül into custody. Now she is  deleting them. She is deleting these  photos. Before the eyes of Turkey, the  biggest scandal, the biggest corruption , the biggest fraud in the history of  the Republic of Turkey is being  destroyed like this. The perpetrator is  deleting her social media accounts  right before our eyes. She is erasing  the day she pulled off the heist. Then  they say there is justice in Turkey,  there is law in Turkey. "We will get  the money back," and so on. Go ahead  and take it, the law says she has to  pay 4.4 billion TL. You couldn't even  take her statement, you couldn't touch  her. Look, Fonzi Fatma is bigger than  Turkey, that is the essence of the  matter. She proved this. I mean, this  time it was directly proven. Now, in  the same way, during all this, "I can  talk." It’s going from ear to ear.  The leaking of words like "I have  things to tell, I wasn't alone." It  went exactly to the right address. It  reached the exact target. Well, let's  continue. Is that only it? There are  newer connections, very recent scandals . Osman Arıkan Nacar. Osman Arıkan  Nacar. Very important. Former  bureaucrat. He was a parliamentary  candidate nominee twice for the AKP. He  really wants to be a member of  parliament. He couldn't, but he is one  of the sweet, very sweet bureaucrats of  the AKP government. Do you know what he  did? 20 billion Turkish Lira. He  swindled 20 billion Lira from the fund  and fled abroad. A fugitive. 20 billion . Look, Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya had 2  billion. This one is 20 billion, 20  billion TL. How many trucks would it  fill? I mean, we have this studio here  now. Just like this studio. If we had 3  more studios and filled them with money , it would just barely fill up. It  wouldn't even fill. The guy swindled 20  billion TL and ran away. 20 billion TL.  Osman Arıkan Nacar. So, Osman Arıkan  Nacar. What does Arıkan Nacar do for a  living? He held positions as one of the  most important AKP bureaucrats:  Ministry of Health Pharmaceutical and  Medical Device Agency, Head of the  Medical Device Department, General  Directorate of Emergency Health  Services, and President of the Turkish  Medicines and Medical Devices Agency.  He became Deputy Undersecretary at the  Ministry of Labor and Social Security.  Then, while still a bureaucrat, he  became a candidate in the 2015  elections. He wasn't included on the  list. He returned to bureaucracy. He  became a Deputy Undersecretary again.  He is that well-liked. He was that big  of an AKP figure. The government is  wrong. He resigned again on April 24,  2018. He applied for candidacy from the  AKP again. He couldn't become a  candidate again. Look, we are talking  about a civil servant, friends. A civil  servant and medical devices related to  our health, medicines, and their  reimbursements. The Ministry of Labor  and Social Security handles these  reimbursements, right? Insurance. The  person who handles these, meaning the  Deputy Undersecretary of the Ministry  of Social Security. He serves as a  deputy undersecretary. His older  brother is the Adana Provincial Health  Director, Halil Nacar. This person  carried out a 20 billion TL swindle. He  is a fugitive abroad, and Zeynel Emre  also revealed recently that he was on  vacation in Bodrum with Ömer Çelik.  This is a major swindler. A 20 billion  TL swindler. How can I explain 20  billion TL? Look, let me explain it  this way. Let me repeat what I said in  the last broadcast. Şişli's  infrastructure was renewed. There is a  banner. 2.1 billion TL. They renewed  the infrastructure of all of Şişli,  Istanbul Şişli. Now think about this:  20 billion TL. I mean, you could almost  renew the infrastructure of Istanbul.  The man took it all by himself. He is a  fugitive abroad. Now, this...Exactly.  This man also has partners. Look, it's  very interesting. Really very  interesting. He is a fugitive now, he  is being sought. We don't know if he is  missing or being sought. What did he do  with the money? The money is abroad.  How does the money get out, my friend?  Look, it's the same situation as with  Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya. Where did she  find 163 million TL? Just to put into a  fund. Houses appeared, villas appeared,  mansions appeared, all sorts of things  appeared. Now, if this man swindled 20  billion TL, just think about the money  he put into that fund. If there is a transfer,  there must be an election. And it  turned out how the election would take  place. They took Murat Güneş into  custody and arrested him last night.  Look, do you know how it is in law  actually? Arresting an innocent person,  arresting an innocent person is a big,  how should I say it? It is where  justice ends. I mean, everyone here  knows that Murat Güneş is innocent.  You are putting a person in jail just  to seat an AKP member in that mayoral  chair. Then his child is saddened, his  wife cries, his mother cries, his  father cries, and those people are  devastated. I mean, why will an AKP  member sit in that chair? They do not  value human beings. And the one sitting  in that chair will portray themselves  as an elected mayor. What did you do?  You changed the balance of the council,  you made transfers. You arrested the  mayor. Not just the mayor, they also  arrested three members. A total of 13  people were in custody, and you  arrested them too. You will enter the  council member election. We won. Then  you will go around claiming to be the  mayor. Just like Serkan Bayram, the AKP  deputy, said, "We win at the table, you  know. I cannot reconcile this with my  honor. I cannot stomach it with my  pride," he said. But some people  stomach it. Truly, some people stomach  it. Eyüp Sultan Mayor is also Özmen.  Mithat Bülent Özmen was referred to  court with a request for arrest. They  will do that to him too. Democracy is  now very far away. Now, meanwhile,  demonstrations have started in Paris,  in France. Very interesting  developments are happening in the world  there as well. High schools, in a sense , rose up due to unfavorable education  conditions. The events grew very large.  France is like a fire zone in many  cities; they are clashing with the  police. Large-scale protests, the  trouble in France is truly growing  every day. There are also housing  protests in Spain. It has spread to  Belgium, and it is said that the  protests in France do not resemble  those in the past and are much more  violent. See you tomorrow. Goodbye. H

items.title: Cemil Tugay| Mustafa Sandal| İoanna Kuçuradi - Yılmaz Özdil
items.transkript: Hello. The agenda is burning hot. Today  we will continue talking about Fonzi.  As you know, there are two couples who  left their mark on the Fonzi scandal.  One is our Minister of Family Affairs,  Fatma Hanım, and her husband. The  other is Mustafa Sandal and his wife. I  will tell you a very interesting detail  about this. A detail that has never  been talked about, that you have never  heard anywhere. Also, in my broadcast  last Friday, I talked about the Ponzi  schemers 'love for Finland, and how our  Minister of Family Affairs, Fatma  Betül Sayan Kaya, had connections to  Finland and the book "In the Land of  White Lilies." I told the story of how  Finland, a country of swamps,  transformed into a land of white lilies –a story Atatürk recommended to this  country–and how this transformation  happened in Türkiye. Following that  broadcast, I received many messages,  especially from young people. They are  asking if a similar event to Fonzi  occurred during the Atatürk era, the  founding years of the Republic. Yes.  Yes, it did. You won't believe your  eyes and ears. Fonzi during Atatürk's  time, and who is it connected to today?  I will explain shortly. The head of the  Central Referee Board, Ferhat Gündoğu , was also arrested. Everyone thinks  this is related to football. They think  it's about referees or betting, or  something like that. But is it? Isn't  this issue right at the heart of the  Fethullah Gülen movement issue? Right  at the heart. We'll be talking about  that today. Also, İzmir Metropolitan  Municipality Mayor Cemil Tugay resigned  from the CHP. Last week he went to the  palace to thank our leader of the  century. It's being claimed that  tomorrow he will join the AKP with a  badge from our leader of the century.  When I was recording this broadcast, it  was still just a claim. The AKP in  İzmir was only a dream. It was a  fantasy, but it will become reality. So  today we will be discussing this issue  in light of forgotten truths. We lost  Iona Kuçuradi. The world's largest  family. She's not someone who can be  dismissed with a trivial tweet of "oh  dear, our condolences." Iona,  especially for our valuable young  people, I will tell you something  completely different, something you've  never heard before. It will be a  mini-documentary you will never forget.  But first of all, what is today? Today  is October 6th. The liberation of  Istanbul is a very important day. A day  of remembrance for those who celebrate  the conquest of Istanbul but not its  liberation. Mehmet conquered, Mehmet VI  lost. Mustafa Kemal Atatürk liberated.  This is an unchangeable truth. Look at  those friends who don't celebrate the  liberation of Istanbul to avoid  remembering Atatürk with gratitude and  respect. Let me remind you of some  photos for nostalgia. For example, look  at the first photo from the special  preparation, for example, I'm asking my  esteemed editor Erdi. Erdi, let's bring  just one. This is photo number one.  This is Istiklal Street. The heart of  Istanbul. The occupying forces are  parading through Beyoğlu. In the  streets of Istanbul, there were not  only British, French, and Greeks, but  also Italians, Americans, Algerians,  Moroccans, and Indians. Even Japanese  soldiers were patrolling Istanbul. Look  at photo number 2. In front of  Dolmabahçe Palace and Dolmabahçe  Mosque. The occupying battleships are  operating in the Bosphorus almost like  city ferry boats. Not only British and  French destroyers were in the Bosphorus , but also Italian and Greek ones. And  at the same time, American, Spanish,  and Japanese ships supporting the  occupation were anchored in the Sea of  Marmara. Yes. Even Spain and Japan  wanted a piece of the pie. Photo number  3. Our Sultan and his puppets were  watching like fools. The Galata Tower,  the British flag was waving at the top  of the Galata Tower. Photo number 4.  British soldiers. From the watchtower  perched on top of the Galata Tower,  they are watching those who are  watching them like fools through  binoculars. They are watching Istanbul  through binoculars. Photo number 5.  Look, this is the Golden Horn. The  Golden Horn, a British submarine. Photo  number 6. A British gendarme. He is  checking the identities of our people  in our own land, in our own city. He  says, "Who are you?""Let me see your ID ." And photo number 7. Please look very  carefully at this picture. A patriotic  member of the National Forces was  captured while crossing from Istanbul  to Anatolia. He was tied to a mast in  the shipyard yard in Kocaeli. He is  being shot dead by a Greek detachment  in our own country. Yes. Please look  carefully at the photograph. The  Ottoman official, wearing a fez, is  also overseeing this execution along  with the occupying British officer.  Today is the 6th of October anniversary . Celebrating the conquest of Istanbul  but not celebrating the liberation of  Istanbul is not just Atatürk animosity . It is also proof of how much the  puppets of imperialism, the puppets of  imperialism, miss the imperialist  occupation, as shown in these  photographs I have shown. They miss it.  Please lean back and close your eyes.  Yes. If you are driving, pull over.  Never mind, just be a little late for  work. Shall I take you back to those  days? Today is a special day. Let me  bring it to life in your mind with a  5-6 minute mini-documentary. Please  close your eyes. Before October 6th,  that is, before the liberation of  Istanbul, the name of Istanbul was  Constantinople. Yes. Its population was  806,000 people. There were only about  100,000 houses. They were all made of  wood. Fires were a huge problem. When  the fire started, the fate of the  neighborhood was determined by the  mercy of the wind. There were only  about 400 apartment buildings in total.  Everything after Şişli was outside  the city. Mecidiyeköy, as its name  suggests, was truly a village. There  were only 34 houses in gardens. The  rest were mulberry groves. Etiler was  like a remote mountain area. In the  winter months, wolves would come down  to Etiler. American flour, Dutch sugar,  and English rice were sold. Local  production was zero. Hotels, the hotels  in Istanbul, didn't accept Ottoman  currency. They worked with British  pounds in Istanbul. After October 6th,  after the liberation of Istanbul, that  is, after Constantinople became  Istanbul. Yes. Mustafa Kemal Atatürk  made Istanbul what it is today. Now,  those who call themselves "new Ottomans " should listen carefully. Even the  Ottomans called it Constantinople.  Including Fatih Sultan Mehmet. Look at  the coins of all the sultans from 1453  onwards. It says Constantinople.  Mustafa Kemal Atatürk made  Constantinople, Constantinople, into  Istanbul. An official letter was sent  to the International Postal Service. It  was announced that from now on, the  names of Turkish cities would be in  Turkish. Letters addressed as " Constantinople" were not delivered. The  whole world had to obediently write " Istanbul." They had to say "Istanbul."  Immediately after October 6th, the  Opera Cinema opened in Beyoğlu. Yes.  Locals were covered in red carpet.  There were ushers in fancy white gloves . Immediately afterwards, the Melek  Cinema opened. It had baroque-decorated  boxes. It was closed every evening.  Istanbul was transforming. The Loran  pastry shop opened. Yes. It was the  pronunciation of the French word Lorien , meaning east. The owner wasn't  actually French. It was Filipos  Lenastı. He was a Greek citizen. This  Loran pastry shop, which is as old as  the Republic, later changed its name to  Baylan. Yes, today's Baylan. The  Turkish people first tasted espresso,  cappuccino, milkshake, and tiramiso  there. Baylan is the beginning of  everything. There were curtains on  public transport vehicles like ferries  and trams. Yes. Women sat behind the  curtain. They couldn't even sit next to  their teachers. After the liberation of  Istanbul, those curtains were lifted.  Topkapi Palace was turned into a museum . For 400 years it belonged to the  sultans. From October 6th onwards, from  the liberation of Istanbul, it belonged  to the people. It was a cultural  turning point. The Istanbul port was  nationalized. Before October 6th, the  French hadn't seized it. We paid for it  within the legal framework. We bought  back our own property, which the  Ottoman Palace had practically given  away like a fountain, from other  countries with our own money. A Karpiç  restaurant opened on Istanbul Street.  It was opened by Yuri Karpatov, who had  fled the Bolshevik revolution and come  to Istanbul. Its menu offered Russian  and French cuisine. Customers without  ties were not accepted. The waiters  wore tuxedos. Later, at Atatürk's  request, a branch was opened in Ankara.  The first Turkish operetta was staged  at the Şehbal Theatre in Kadıköy.  Yes. The name was "Ballroom Fugitives."  Ballroom Fugitives. The first Turkish  operetta caused a sensation. The  leading role was played by soprano  Suzan Lütfullah. The first Turkish  Madonna. Suzan Lütfullah was only 17  years old. She was Gülli Suruni's  mother. From October 6th onwards, the  hat fashion began among our women. Yes.  Women, freed from the veil, the curtain , the cage, saw the hat, which  partially covered their hair, as a kind  of savior. Models from Paris, London,  and New York began arriving in Istanbul . The first New Year's Eve ball of the  Republic of Turkey was held at the Pera  Palace on the night connecting 1925 and  1926. Türkiye's first New Year's Eve  fish restaurant, the Karl Man Passage,  opened on İstiklal Street. It had  everything from perfumery to shoes,  bags to underwear, coats to fabrics,  carpets to furniture. In fact, the Karl  Man Passage was the ancestor of today's  shopping malls. The Istanbul  Municipality purchased its first  municipal buses in 1926. Until then,  passengers were only transported by  tram. Four Renault Sikemia models were  purchased. They were imported from  France, of course. Their bodies were  wooden. They had a capacity of 30  people each. They started operating on  the Beyazıt-Eminönü route. Istanbul  Radio began broadcasting. For example,  our first radio station was primarily  music. There was a news bulletin under  the name "Ajans"(Agency). Charlie Stone  was fashionable among young people.  Dance classes began to open in Istanbul . From the liberation of Istanbul  onwards, the most famous ballroom in  Istanbul on warm summer nights was the  Summer Place hotel in Tarabya. It was  legendary. As news of such balls in  Istanbul was published in newspapers,  it encouraged Anatolia as well. Balls  spread to cities in Anatolia too. The  first Gazi Race was held in Ankara, but  it was won by Ali Muhittin Hacıbekir's  purebred horse named Neriman.  Hacıbekir was both very rich and very  much a womanizer. There were rumors  that he even paid women to light their  cigarettes. The horse's name was  Neriman. So, Neriman, who won the first  Gazi Race, was actually the name of a  woman he had a romantic relationship  with, right? Neriman was actually the  wife of a very famous journalist in the  Istanbul press. In those days, gossip  news wasn't as open as it is today. It  was considered taboo. Such insinuations  were made in a more discreet way. But  everyone actually knew very well what  the headlines about Neriman meant. A  tasting restaurant opened. Its owner  was an Italian named Eduardo Morigini.  Yes. It was a first in our history. A  tasting restaurant. Because he brought  Italian cuisine to Istanbul Street,  Istiklal Street. Yes. Italian cuisine  on Istiklal Street. The tasting  restaurant. Its pasta was the talk of  the whole city. Italian wines were  served. Eduardo Morigini. Electricity  came to Kadıköy. Yes. Before the  liberation of Istanbul, there was no  electricity in Kadıköy. The Süreya  Opera opened in Kadıköy. The Süreya  operetta was established. Who was in  the cast? Şevkiye May, Samiha Semiha  Berksoy, Suzan Sururi, Toto Karaca,  Nezaat Diligil. There are legends.  Before the liberation of Istanbul,  before the Republic, Turkish women, who  were even forbidden from appearing on  stage, were now dazzling not only in  Türkiye but also on European stages.  The Istanbul City Theatre was  established. After the liberation of  Istanbul, the people of Istanbul began  to become acquainted with the works of  Shakespeare, Schiller, Molière, and  Chekhov. Citizens flocked to the  theater. For example, while Istanbul's  population was only 806,000, 50,000  spectators attended the theater  annually. Social life in Istanbul  exploded like fireworks. Something  unprecedented happened, not just in  Türkiye, but in the world: a woman  became the captain of the men's  volleyball team. Sabiha became the  captain of the Fenerbahçe men's  volleyball team. They became champions  undefeated. Türkiye's first automobile  factory was established in Tophane. Yes , the American Ford Motor Company. They  produced 45 cars every month.  Türkiye's first traffic lights were  installed in Karaköy. Türkiye's first  tailoring school opened in Istanbul.  Turkish women became acquainted with  cosmetic products after the liberation  of Istanbul. Yes, skincare products  like creams, powders, and nail polish  began to be used. Istanbul had famous  hairdressers. German, Max; French, Bazi ; Russian, George; French, Marcel. With  the liberation of Istanbul, Turks began  both going to hairdressers and becoming  hairdressers themselves. Yes. There  weren't even any Turkish hairdressers  before. Feria Tevfik, from Istanbul,  was chosen as the first Miss Turkey in  our history through a competition in  Istanbul. Feria Tevfik represented  Türkiye in the Miss Universe  competition in California, USA. A  telephone connection was established  between Istanbul and Ankara. Harley  Davidson motorcycles arrived in  Istanbul. The dealership was in Galata.  From the first October 6th, that is,  from the liberation of Istanbul, modern  furniture stores began to open. Modern.  Modern was the magic word. It was like  the password of liberation and the  republic. Modern lifestyle was changing . Homes were changing. Furniture was  changing. Furniture was being  advertised in newspapers for the first  time. Yes. Chandeliers, lampshades,  wall sconces, etc., which were only  found in palaces and mansions before  the Republic, were now in the homes of  ordinary citizens. This is the  liberation of Istanbul. Pressure cooker  advertisements started, for example.  Mulein Rouge opened in Beyoğlu. It  suddenly became the most popular  entertainment venue in Istanbul.  Eftalya the Mermaid performed there.  Safiye Ayla performed there. It was the  first casino to bring Müzeyyen Senar  to the stage. Gülen Ruş. The Galata  Bridge was made free. From the  liberation of Istanbul onwards. Yes.  Now our esteemed national government is  making us pay for a bridge we don't  even use. Conversely, the toll bridge  was made free. For 85 years, a toll was  collected for crossing the Galata  Bridge. Pedestrians paid 20 para,  porters 40 para. Empty cars paid 2  kuruş, loaded cars 5 kuruş. It was  made free after the liberation of  Istanbul. The districts of Galatasaray,  Kadıköy, Beşiktaş, Fatih, Eminönü , and Sarıyer were established. Yes.  Before the liberation of Istanbul,  until Atatürk liberated Istanbul,  there was no address in Istanbul  bearing the title of Fatih Sultan  Mehmet. Atatürk established the Fatih  district. The districts of Kadıköy,  Beşiktaş, Eminönü, and Sarıyer  were established. We started drinking  soda after the liberation of Istanbul.  It didn't exist before. Newspapers ran  health-focused advertisements for sodas . They claimed it was good for the  stomach, made from fruit, and very  foamy. They said drinking it before tea  in the morning was a laxative, and  drinking too much was a purgative. The  sweetened version was said to be as  delicious as champagne. This nation  only discovered and tasted soda after  the liberation of Istanbul. Not only in  Türkiye, but the world's first  children's rights rally was organized  in Istanbul thanks to the efforts of  teacher Nakiye Elgün. Yes. Children  held banners. They wrote about not  being beaten, not being frightened, not  being scolded, respect, compassion,  mother's milk, sleeping alone, air and  sun, and gardens that belonged to us. I  was writing these demands on the  banners in the children's hands. The  National Education Vision was hundreds  of years ahead of today's  sectarian-friendly National Education.  After the liberation of Istanbul,  Türkiye's first queen of voices was  chosen. As with the beauty contest,  Cumhuriyet Newspaper organized it. It  was in the Western music category.  Hüdadat Şakir Hanım was chosen first . Actually, she wasn't a singer. She  was married and a mother of one child.  She spoke German and French. She was a  courageous woman of the Republic.  Electricity came to Büyükada. The  Koska liqueur shop opened. Many people  living in Istanbul today don't know  this, but there was a neighborhood  called Koska between Beyazıt and  Laleli. The shop was there. The  Mecidiyeköy Liqueur factory opened.  Liqueur was one of the cornerstones of  industrial heritage. Raspberry, banana,  mint, apricot, strawberry, bitter  almond, lemon, sour cherry, orange, and  tangerine liqueurs were produced. The  tradition of offering liqueur with  coffee became a part of Turkish culture . Yes. It entered our lives with this  factory. How is it going? Is the  liberation of Istanbul going well?  Don't open your eyes. Let's continue.  The first sound film of Turkish cinema,  titled "Istanbul Streets," was shot in  Istanbul. It was the story of two  brothers who fall in love with the same  woman in the streets of Istanbul. The  director was Muhsin Ertuğrul. The film  starred actors like Semiha Berksoy and  Hazım Körmükçü. It was actually  filmed silently. The voice-over was  done in Paris. It was the story of two  brothers who were in love with the same  woman. The woman was a cabaret singer.  One of the brothers was a banker. He  mixed his work with his love life. He  embezzled the bank's money and spent it  with his singer girlfriend. When the  bank discovered the situation, he was  fired and his family was deprived of  the embezzled money. The family went  bankrupt. And since it was the same  woman, the two brothers were already at  odds with each other. They fought.  During the fight, one brother went  blind. Yes. A lot of money was needed  for the surgery. Then the wealthy uncle  passed away. A magnificent mansion was  left as an inheritance. A glimmer of  hope appeared, but unfortunately, a  fire broke out and the mansion became  unusable. Luckily, towards the end of  the film, a wealthy and benevolent  woman unexpectedly appeared, paid for  the surgery, reconciled the two  brothers, and they returned to their  happy lives. This film broke box office  records. And do you know why I  described this film in so much detail?  The film "Istanbul Streets" wasn't just  unique because it was our first sound  film. It was the starting point for all  the Yeşilçam clichés: naive rich  young men falling prey to bad women,  brothers becoming enemies because of  women, people going blind for no reason , miraculously recovering, happy  endings, and so on. Yes. Written by  Muhsin Ertuğrul, this film was full of  Yeşilçam clichés and would be remade  thousands of times with different  actors but the same subject matter. In  Istanbul, there was a pharmacy called  Hasan Eczane. Hasan Eczane was 100  years ahead of its time. Yes. Because  it produced gluten-free bread.  Unbelievable! It was freshly made every  day. Hasan Eczane advertised with its  brand name. It was sold with the slogan  "Against diabetes." It was claimed to  be prepared according to the formula  accepted as food for diabetics by the  last EtiBA Congress. It was said to  scientifically help overweight people  lose weight without weakening them. As  I said, Pharmacist Hasan was truly  ahead of his time. They were producing  diabetic sugar, diabetic chocolate,  diabetic biscuits. They were producing  gluten-free pasta. The pharmacy was  producing lentil flour, pea flour.  Pharmacist Hasan was amazing. After the  liberation of Istanbul, Chevrolet came  to Istanbul. Yes, Fisk tires came. Ford  came. Ford had practically monopolized  the truck market. After the liberation  of Istanbul, the nightlife of the  Turkish people began. Before, it didn't  exist. The entertainment sector became  a source of advertising for newspapers.  For example, there were concerts in  Küçük Çiftlik Park, Harbiye Belbü,  Sarayburnu Park, Taksim Panorama Garden , and Bebek Garden. Every night, around  15 venues in Istanbul were hosting  musical nights. Each one attracted  customers by advertising separately.  Beach advertisements exploded in the  summer. Yes. The most popular beach was  Kız Kulesi beach. Kız Kulesi beach.  It wasn't just sea and sun on the  beaches. There was entertainment too.  For example, there was a concert by  Hikmet Rıza Hanım at Kız Kulesi  beach. There was jazz orchestra and  dancing. The concept of discounts  entered our lives with the liberation  of Istanbul. It was a  certificate from a madrasa. An  elementary school diploma from a  madrasa. With this document, it was  impossible for him to enroll in any  school in Türkiye. Despite this,  Atatürk's Republic...The old Turkey,  which they disliked, helped him. The  Istanbul National Education Directorate  helped him. He was enrolled in an Imam  Hatip school as a guest student. He was  registered under the name Mehmet  Alioğlu, that was his name at the time . He even became a classmate of Tayyip  Erdoğan at that Imam Hatip school.  They met there. He finished Imam Hatip  school. He took the university entrance  exam. His score was barely enough for  that place. Where? Atatürk University,  Faculty of Agriculture, Zoology  Department. If he hadn't gotten in  there, he would have become a zoologist . A year later, he transferred to the  Faculty of Literature. A year later, he  transferred to the Faculty of Law. So,  miraculous things were happening. He  wasn't passing the exam, but his  faculty was improving. Another miracle  happened. The state provided him with a  great opportunity. It said," Since you  are a Greek citizen, a foreign national , you can take the foreign nationals ' exam. "Now, the scores for Turkish  citizens and foreign nationals are not  the same. If you answer even half as  many questions correctly as Turkish  citizens, you get a higher score than  Turkish citizens. Şark entered  Istanbul University's Cerrahpaşa  Faculty of Medicine. He had barely  managed to get into Atatürk  University's Zoology program. Hampaan  entered Türkiye's most prestigious  medical faculty. He became a doctor. He  got his diploma from Cerrahpaşa. He  rushed back to Greece. He rushed back,  but Greece didn't even treat him like a  human being. They didn't allow him to  work as a doctor. So, he changed  direction again. He secretly crossed  the Meriç River. He fled to Atatürk's  Republic as an illegal immigrant. He  fled to that old Türkiye they disliked . Are you listening carefully? When he  fled to Türkiye as a Greek citizen,  Greece immediately stripped him of his  citizenship. Yes. Stateless. What does  that mean? He became stateless. He  wandered around as a stateless person  for 3 years. Did he think he could find  an opportunity to go to another country , or was he thinking he could return to  Greece someday? I don't know. He lived  as a stateless person in Türkiye for 3  years. He resided as a stateless person  for 3 years. Then, for some reason, I  don't know...He decided to become a  citizen. He applied. The Republic of  Turkey, the very Turkey they looked  down upon as" old Turkey, "did not  reject him. It gave him a homeland. It  gave him a Turkish Republic identity  card. He became a citizen of the  Republic of Turkey. He didn't even have  a surname. When he came from Greece, he  was just Mehmet. When he enrolled in  the Imam Hatip school, they asked for  his father's name. When he said Ali, it  was written as Mehmet Aliğlu. In 1986,  when he received his Turkish Republic  identity card, for the first time in  his life, at the age of 31, he truly  had a surname. He took the surname  Müezzinoğlu. Mehmet Müezzinoğlu  became a citizen, an individual, a  doctor, a state doctor, a hospital  owner, a member of parliament, a  minister, and the Minister of Health in  the parliamentary system that he  disliked, the Türkiye they looked down  upon in" old Türkiye, "a country he  disliked because of the regime  established by Atatürk. He went to  Greece, from which he had been stripped  of his citizenship, with a Turkish  Republic passport. He was able to pray  Friday prayers in the mosque in his  ancestral homeland, a place he could  never set foot in again, thanks to his  Turkish Republic passport. Everything  he gained in his life, he gained thanks  to the Republic of Turkey. But his  ministerial position, the Ministry of  Health...As soon as he took office as  minister, what was the first thing he  did? He had the" TC "(Republic of  Turkey) designation removed from the  Ministry of Health. Yes. As soon as he  became minister, he had the" TC " designation removed from his ministry.  That wasn't enough. In 2024, as you may  remember, the newborn baby scandal  erupted. It's impossible to forget. It  was revealed that a gang, devoid of  humanity, had colluded with some  private hospitals to rob the state,  deliberately causing the deaths of  newborn babies solely to profit from  the state. Which private hospital,  whose license was revoked and which was  closed because of this collaboration,  was it? It turned out to be the  hospital of former Health Minister  Mehmet Müezzinoğlu. The private  Avcılar Hospital. One is a Turkish  citizen of Greek origin, the other a  Greek of Turkish origin. Yes. Ionla  Kuçuradi, despite everything that  happened to her from childhood, despite  having her property confiscated by the  Wealth Tax, despite being practically  expelled from the country after the  1967 events and the May 27th coup,  never held a grudge against this  country; she worked, produced, educated , taught, and...One is a Turkish  citizen of Greek origin who has  contributed beauty to Türkiye to the  very last breath. The other is a Greek  woman of Turkish origin who became a  citizen, a doctor, a member of  parliament, and a minister thanks to  this country. I chose to describe Iona  Kuçuradi this way so that you can feel  her importance both in your mind and in  your heart. This is being discussed a  lot now with the opening issue. The  concept of citizenship. What does it  mean to love one's country? What does  it mean to love one's nation? What is  the vision of humane living, which is  the founding philosophy of the Republic  of Turkey? What is constitutional  citizenship? What does it mean to say"  I am proud to be a Turk "? Iona  Kuçuradi was that. And finally, Izmir.  Izmir Metropolitan Municipality Mayor  Cemil Tugay resigned from the CHP. Last  week, he went to the palace and thanked  our leader repeatedly. It is claimed  that tomorrow he will defect to the AKP  with the badge that our leader will  give him. When I was filming this  broadcast, it was still just a claim.  The AKP could only dream of Izmir. The  dream is becoming reality. I mean, I  will never forget. It was February 12,  2003. February 12 2003. There was a  Turkey-Ukraine national football match  in Izmir. A friendly match between our  national football teams. Turkey vs.  Ukraine, February 12, 2003. Our leader  was still politically banned. The AKP  had come to power alone, but our leader  was still politically banned. Prime  Minister Abdullah Gül had just won the  Siirt elections, which had been  cancelled. The Siirt elections were to  be held again in March, a month later,  and Tayyip Erdoğan was certain to be  elected as a member of parliament and  become prime minister. That was certain . But on February 12, 2003, he was  still politically banned. Representing  our leader, Prime Minister Abdullah  Gül, along with about 10 ministers,  government ministers, and AKP MPs from  Izmir, came to Izmir for this special  national match in a show of force, and  an unprecedented protest occurred in  the history of the Republic, unlike  anything seen in sporting events up to  that point. Many such incidents  happened later, but this was the first.  They were surrounded by 50,000 people  filling the stands of the Izmir  Atatürk Stadium. Yes. The AKP  government, who came to Izmir to watch  the match, were watching from the VIP  binoculars...He was shocked." Brother,  you've come to power alone. 50,000  people are cheering you on. "They  cheered and booed for minutes. Very  harsh slogans were shouted. It was the  first major mass reaction in Türkiye  after the AKP came to power alone.  İzmir. This event was the turning  point for the AKP-İzmir match. A  turning point. Look, you know that  İzmir isn't actually CHP-centric?  İzmir isn't right-wing, nor is it  left-wing. Look, the Democratic Party  won elections in that city. The Justice  Party won. Of course, the CHP won, the  DSP won, the SHP won, the DP won, the  ANAP won. But İzmir is, in the truest  sense of the word, a bastion of modern  life. Look, that's its red line. It's a  city where the sea is like a girl, the  girl is like the sea, and the streets  smell of both girls and the sea. People  from all 81 cities live in İzmir. The  cement that binds them all together is  Atatürk. İzmir is Mustafa Kemal's  soldier. Show them Atatürk's picture.  Our women will cry and hear his name.  From Kadifekale to Avra Street, from  Tilkilik to Karantina...From  Karşıyaka to Güzelyalı, from Susuz  Dede to Hocazade Mosque, from Tenekeli  Neighborhood to Agora, from our  Afro-Turks to our Kurdish-Turks, our  Levantines, mosques, synagogues,  temples, mosques, synagogues, churches  stand side by side in peace. It is the  very essence of the Republic. İzmir,  with the names of its streets and  squares, is a museum of the National  Struggle. İzmir is a museum of the  National Struggle. We value not just  being born or living in İzmir, but  looking at life like an İzmirian, a  shared mentality. An Ardahan resident  who looks at life like an İzmirian is  an İzmirian. A Trabzon resident is an  İzmirian. A Hakkari resident is an  İzmirian. A Antalya resident is an  İzmirian. A Çorum resident is an  İzmirian. A Yozgat resident is an  İzmirian. We value shared mentality.  We value a contemporary way of life.  This is actually the reason why İzmir  is anti-AKP. It's not a mosaic. İzmir  is a marbled paper. We would never want  it to be damaged or spoiled. That's why  the match between AKP and İzmir has  been going on since 2002. I remember it  clearly, it was 2005. Tayyip Erdoğan  said it at a meeting of AKP provincial  chairmen, or something like that. He  said," Hopefully, İzmir will shed some  of the labels attached to it in the  first election. "That's how he sees it.  He meant to say" Infidel İzmir. "They  later made 50 statements to correct  that statement. İzmir never forgets it . Actually, the term" Infidel İzmir " isn't an insult, you know? The people  of İzmir themselves gave it that label . They call the people of İzmir"  Infidel İzmir. "But it was the people  of İzmir who coined the term. Because  Alsancak, during the Ottoman period,  was a neighborhood inhabited only by  non-Muslims. And among the non-Muslims,  there were all kinds of people.  Belgians, Italians, French, they were  all there. Its name back then was Punta . When Turks living in the İki  Çeşmeli or Bayraklı areas went to  Punta, they would say," We're going to  Infidel İzmir. "So," Infidel "didn't  actually refer to religion. It was a  geographical description. A way of  giving directions. And what about the  AKP? For 25 years, they couldn't even  grasp this. Özgür Özel, as a Turk,  did what the AKP couldn't do in 25  years. Yes. I won't repeat myself.  Those who follow me know. I practically  tore myself apart warning about this  before the 2024 elections. Even Cemil  Tugay must have been surprised that he  was made the İzmir Metropolitan  Municipality mayoral candidate. Özgür  Özel couldn't interfere in Istanbul,  which was already under Ekrem  İmamoğlu's control. He couldn't get a  grip on Mansur Yavaş in Ankara. He  came to İzmir. He destroyed İzmir.  Özgür took revenge on İzmir. He  thought he could easily use the types  who switched to the AKP–the  prostitutes, the bribe-takers. He made  them all mayors in İzmir. The AKP  could never win İzmir. With these  choices, Özgür Özel gifted İzmir to  the AKP with his own hands. The  dishonorable, shameless hired  journalists, who are on the payroll of  the party and now appear in the  so-called opposition media, sold İzmir  to the AKP. They sold it. İzmir came  to these Cemil Tugays. I don't know who , but they all received awards from  this current municipality. They gave  conferences. They took the money. They  returned to Izmir and sold it to the  AKP. They are Özgür Özel's puppets.  But as an Izmir resident, I can't help  but say this: The AKP is happy right  now, but the game isn't over in Izmir  yet. We are here. You can transfer  puppets, but you can't transfer the  people. The game isn't over in Izmir  yet. That's all for today. Please don't  forget to subscribe, like, comment, and  share. I will be holding a raffle among  my subscribers. I will be giving away  books by Iona Kuçuradi, a gift from  God to this country, to 10 lucky  viewers. See you Friday morning. Thanks . M

items.name: Murat Yetkin
items.title: AK Parti saflarında fon krizi çatlakları. - Murat Yetkin
items.transkript: Hello everyone. My respects and best  wishes to you all. The fund crisis  continues. The stock market crisis  continues and is deepening. As it  deepens, new developments emerge.  Questions are also being asked about  why more isn't coming out. I will touch  upon those as well. What kind of  developments happened over the weekend?  For example, regarding the previous  chairman of the Capital Markets Board,  İbrahim Ömer Gönül, there were  rumors and very serious allegations  that he was delaying these matters. He  was even replaced, I believe on May 9th . His deputy, Mahmut Sütçü, was  appointed in his place. We can say that  the same team is effectively continuing , just with a change in leadership.  Anyway. The Istanbul Chief Public  Prosecutor's Office requested  permission to investigate. From where?  From the Ministry of Treasury and  Finance. Minister of Treasury and  Finance Mehmet Şimşek did not grant  the request for an investigation, but  assigned the inspection board, citing  the need to act according to  regulations. Now, we can say this is  the first high-level bureaucrat against  whom action has been taken due to this  fund crisis. Who was the first  politician? Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya.  Now, very strange statements are  emerging regarding Fatma Betül Sayan  Kaya. One is from journalist Hadi  Özışık. Hadi Özışık says, "I  spoke with her." He says he learned  what she could disclose, but she told  him, "For God's sake, don't tell anyone ." That's why I'm not telling. Well  then, why did he attempt such a thing?  He says, "I'm not looking for clicks."  Hadi Özışık. Deniz Zeyrek said  something like this on his YouTube  channel. This is quite different, of  course. Supposedly, she told those in  her close circle, "If the prosecutor  takes my statement, I will tell  everything." Now, this is such a  statement that, I'm serious, it sounds  almost like blackmail. Like, "If the  prosecutor takes my statement, watch  out, I'll name names," and so on. In  the meantime, of course, many of our  journalist colleagues have started  talking about a VIP list. Abdülkadir  Selvi, Deniz Zeyrek, Nevşin Mengü,  and other friends are also doing so. So , supposedly, a list of 5,000 people  was given to President Tayyip Erdoğan.  But 50 of these are allegedly the big  winners, described as profiteers. But  there is also a list of 26 people, who  are allegedly directly linked to the  Justice and Development Party. We keep  using "allegedly" and hearsay. Look,  there is nothing concrete. Because I  just said something very important  based on Deniz Zeyrek's report. I mean,  why is the prosecutor not seeking a  statement from Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya,  or why isn't the Capital Markets Board  filing a criminal complaint? There are  other allegations regarding Fatma  Betül Sayan Kaya, the former Justice  and Development Party minister and  general vice chair who was forced to  resign. For example, questions are  starting to be raised about whether her  medical degree exists or is valid. So,  there is a multi-dimensional situation.  But for some reason, prosecutors are  not inviting her to give a statement.  They aren't even inviting her as a  witness. And about whether she invested  that money or not, that 2.2 billion,  Vahap Munyar, the journalist and  manager of Ekonomim Newspaper, said, " We trust our sources; she did invest it ." So, who can we learn this from? From  the Capital Markets Board, right? Or  from the Ministry of Treasury and  Finance. I mean, there’s nothing from  there either. Where am I trying to get  at with this? Here is where I'm getting  at. Naturally, this caused different  opinions to emerge within the Justice  and Development Party. It led to some  cracks. Now, as soon as we say "cracks, " a denial will follow. No, we are one  and whole. We are doing everything  together. When I say AK Party circles,  I don't mean just the chairman. I don't  mean just the headquarters. Look, there  is a group, for instance, within the  Justice and Development Party circles.  This group is led by Akit columnist and  editor-in-chief Ali Karahasanoğlu. He  says, to summarize, there is no such  thing. This is a CIA and Mossad  conspiracy, the Zionist lobby is at  work, foreign powers did this. They are  slandering the AK Party members. Then  there is the group that says, "Let's  face the facts." Şamil Tayyar. He is  the leader, like a spokesperson for  this. He says, "My brother, let's face  these facts.""Look, our own children  did this." I mean, sure, the opposition  is fanning the flames. The opposition  is trying to do something, I don't know . I'm just relaying this, but our  children did this. He says, "The  children of our own neighborhood." He  says it exactly like that. So, let's  face this reality. Otherwise, he says,  it will come back to haunt us when  election time comes. Now, it's  interesting that in this second group —the "let's face the facts" team— Serkan Bayram holds a unique place. He  is a Justice and Development Party  deputy from Istanbul. He is also one of  the members in the Turkish Grand  National Assembly who is physically  disabled. Due to a tragic accident he  had when he was young. Now, what did he  say? "We are cutting everything from  everywhere," he said, regarding Fatma  Betül. "We are cutting from retirees,  from the disabled.""Are we cutting it  just so Fatma Betül can eat?" He said.  It even reached a point. He implied  that the "Reis," our President, should  leave this AK Party and found a new one  so we could follow him. But then  someone intervened. I don't know, maybe  Ömer Çelik, the party spokesperson,  said these are just rumors. Following  statements about how we are one and  together, Serkan Bayram made a long  statement saying, "Yes, we are going  through a difficult period." We need to  be together. You know the cliché, " These are the days we need unity and  solidarity the most." Something like  that. So, this shows how delicately  this issue is being handled internally  and how it has led to serious  disagreements. Of course, Hayati  Yazıcı can be considered the number  two of the party. He is one of the two  deputies of President Tayyip Erdoğan.  Efgan Ala is still responsible for  parliamentary relations and other  matters. Hayati Yazıcı is the deputy  chairman for legal and political  affairs of the party, and his son is  Mustafa Yazıcı. Now, an injunction  was first issued on Mustafa Yazıcı's  assets. An hour, almost an hour later,  it was immediately retracted. Uh, when  Hayati Yazıcı was asked about this,  he said, "It's a conspiracy against us,  there's no problem regarding my son's  situation." But then, some other  allegations started to emerge. This  Tera Investment. Tera Investment is at  the center of everything anyway. While  we're on the subject of Tera Investment , let's mention this too. Look, our  journalist friend Erdal Sağlam said  there are 12 names. These closed-end  shares. Closed private shares, meaning  hedge funds, private funds. I apologize . Before these were transferred to  TEFAS—what is TEFAS? Turkey's  Electronic Fund Trading Platform. You  know, before they were transferred here , they played a big game. There might  even be politicians among them. ...he  said. It was disclosed. The opposition  also pressured them. It was disclosed.  No, there were no politicians. They  inflated the prices among themselves.  But the main topic of discussion is  Tera Investment. There is nothing about  Tera Investment. Nothing is being  disclosed. Why isn't it being disclosed ? I mean, we keep asking. Let's ask  again. Are there other politicians  there? Are there high-level bureaucrats , I don't know, deputy ministers, uh,  may I say, governors, district  governors, uh, general managers, or  people like that? Are there also  institutions and organizations there  that have invested money? Are there  journalists or television commentators  there? Look, we're talking about our  own profession. Let those who are  confident speak up, sir. Let those who  are confident say it this way. Let them  say, "I have nothing to do with this."  But we also see in the media that among  journalists, television personalities,  and economic commentators, some are  clearly saying this. They say, "Whoever  it is, let it be revealed." I say it,  for example, don't I? But there are  also those who don't say this. Instead  of saying this, there are also those  who say, "Oh, these are conspiratorial  matters.""We must not fall into the  Zionist trap regarding these matters."  Uh, there are also those who say, " These are being brought up to undermine  the President." However, the  information received is that Erdoğan  is also very angry about this. Some in  the opposition say, "Oh, why did that  come to light?" I don't think he's  angry because they were careless or  anything like that. Because, look,  Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya is in the  United Nations delegation. She is in  Erdoğan's United Nations delegation. I  mean, it crosses one's mind. I mean,  would he have taken her along if he  were informed about such things? But  these things are unpredictable. These  things are unpredictable. We are not in  a position to count anything as proof.  We can count them as signs. I can never  count them as proof. As we said, there  are three important things. There are  groups. One is the work of external  powers. The CIA or Mossad did it. The  Zionists did it. And then, uh, the AK  Party has nothing to do with it. "There  are people under Zionist influence who  have infiltrated us," and so on. Then  there is a team saying, as I gave the  example of Şamil Ayrım. I mean, let's  face the facts. Actually, there are  also AK Party deputies who say this.  Let's face the facts. Let the rotten  apples among us be weeded out. Right?  What did the President say in his  September 29th speech anyway? A cleanup . What does a cleanup mean? It means  there are already unclean things in the  middle by itself. But will Erdoğan  really clean things up? Will the  Ministry of Justice truly get to the  bottom of this? Or, saying "we can't  find enough people to be district  chairs" if we clean house, will they  just weed out those who are exposed and  sweep the rest under the rug, praying  no more crises erupt until the election ? I mean, there is something like that.  As we said. There is also a 3rd group.  The 3rd group is silent, waiting to see  what the "Reis"(Chief) says. This is  the vast majority. Silence is expected.  I mean, on one hand, there's that talk  from the Nationalist Movement Party,  from Devlet Bahçeli. He says whoever  it is, let them come forward. Now, on  one hand, that is being tried. There  are those within the Justice and  Development Party saying this. There  are those around the Justice and  Development Party, in media circles,  and among commentators saying this, but  the vast majority say "let's hope  nothing goes wrong." They say "Let's  see what the Reis will say." They say " Let's see what Erdoğan will say." Now,  is this a—what do they call it— litmus test? I mean, this distinction  is truly a very important one. One team  says, whether they are party members or  not, this is a massive contamination.  This is a huge scandal. It is an  operation to pull the wool over the  citizens 'eyes. It is plain and simple  organized theft. Moreover, this term " organized robbery" was first used in  parliament by Müsavat Dervişoğlu,  the Good Party leader. Today, that too  is spreading. In a group speech in  October-November 2024, he said, "What  is happening in the stock market?""Look , there are big things happening in the  stock market.""A new scandal could  explode." He had already asked back  then why the Capital Markets Board (SPK ) wasn't doing its duty. Maybe it  wasn't heard in the agenda of that time , but some people did say it, folks.  Specifically, on June 23, Morgan  Stanley, the international credit  rating agency...After they said, "Your  stock market is inflating badly, watch  out, something will happen to you.""If  you don't fix it, excuse us," the  Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's  Office also warned them. Who did they  warn? They warned the Istanbul stock  exchange. They warned the SPK. It  didn't happen. Who blocked this? Sir?  Bureaucrats blocked it. We live in  Turkey, folks. We live in Turkey. Do  you think any bureaucrat would do  something like that? We are talking  about those who have malicious intent.  We are not talking about the honest  workers. Right? If they don't believe  they have strong backing—look, I'm  not saying if they have a big  connection—if they don't believe  that's the case. Is it possible for  them to ignore what a minister or  prosecutor says in a time like this? Is  it possible? I don't think so. This is  not a situation that can be brushed off  by saying "Oh sir, Zionists or maybe  FETÖ members infiltrated these  bureaucrats." It must be pursued.  That's why we are saying this. Should  it be pursued? >> Some people are saying, "No, no, it's  not that big of a deal.""It will pass."  We will see, but let us say this. Truly , all eyes are on President Tayyip  Erdoğan. What will he do? I mean, sure , the judiciary is independent, right?  According to the constitution, the  judiciary is very independent. We  aren't even getting into that stuff. I  mean, we are not saying that either,  but all eyes are on Erdoğan, and the  citizens should just rest easy. I don't  mean that saying "we will finish this  job, we will see it through" is  unimportant, but talk is cheap. I mean,  we really need to see words turn into  action. Millions of citizens need to  see it, too. Hoping to be with you  again in a new broadcast, goodbye.

items.name: Fatih Altaylı (Köşe Yazısı)
items.title: Fon dolandırıcılığı seçmene nasıl anlatılıyor!
items.transkript:
Fon dolandırıcılığı seçmene nasıl anlatılıyor!

Gerçekten tıp doktoru mu?

Abbas Hacıosmanoğlu

Başkan adaylarım

Muhalefet partileri, muhalif seçmen ve hatta yerli ve yabancı medyanın önemli bir bölümü, fon yolsuzluğu ve dolandırıcılığının AK Parti iktidarına büyük zarar verdiğini düşünüyor. Ayrıca aynı kesimler, iktidarın, mensuplarının ve pek çok üst düzey isminin de bulaştığı bu rezaletin faturasını ödeyemeyeceğini ve seçmenini kendisinin bu işte masum hatta temiz olduğuna inandıramayacağını düşünüyor.

Ben pek o kanaatte değilim açıkçası.

AK Parti bu meseleyi seçmenine bal gibi anlatır ve işin içinden “kahramanlık öyküsüyle” sıyrılır gibime geliyor.

Çünkü AK Parti seçmeni, bazen ekonomik bağımlılık, bazen de gerçekten aşık olduğu için eşinden ayrılmak istemeyen eşlere benziyor.

Çevrenizde de böyle evlilikler ya da ilişkiler vardır muhtemelen.

Ayrılmak için bin neden vardır ama ayrılmamak için bulunan bir nedene sarılır taraflardan biri.

Ne bileyim, mesela adam alenen aldatıyordur hatta eşi tarafından basılmıştır ama eş özünde ayrılmak istemediği için adamın ilişkisini inkar etmesini ister. Yalan söylediğini biliyordur ama bu yalana, bu inkara inanmak işine gelir.

Çünkü düzeni bozulsun, çocuklar sorun yaşasın, maddi sıkıntıya girsin istemez.

Yeni bir düzen kurmak zordur ve yeni düzenin eskisinden iyi olacağının garantisi yoktur.

AK Parti ile seçmen ilişkisi de işte tam böyle.

Bakın, AK Parti bu fon skandalı ile ilgili seçmene neler söylüyor, WhatsApp gruplarında, kahve sohbetlerinde, ev toplantılarında neler anlatıyor. Hepsi gerçek yazışmalardan alıntı. Okuyun ve görün:

“Fon skandalı hükümete kumpas gibi görünüyor.

YENİ Parti Sözcüsü Zeynel Emre, borsa ve fon skandalına ilişkin ellerindeki bilgi ve belgelerin, yaşanan usulsüzlüklerden rahatsız olan ‘dürüst ve namuslu’ devlet memurlarından geldiğini söylüyor. Sorun şu ki, inanmaya hazır seçmen sayısı giderek azalıyor.
